summary: End-to-end ML platforms provide integrated tooling for the full model lifecycle — data preparation, distributed training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model registry, deployment, and monitoring — which you need when building or customizing your own models, operating at scale with governance requirements, or managing many models in production. If you only need to call a pre-trained foundation model (e.g., via OpenAI, Anthropic, or Bedrock APIs) for inference, a managed platform is usually overkill; the platforms below earn their complexity when you train/fine-tune, require reproducibility and compliance, or orchestrate many pipelines across teams. The market is led by the hyperscaler suites (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML) and Databricks, with specialized MLOps and AutoML tools clustering below them.

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute/storage (instance-hours for training, endpoints, notebooks); no upfront fees; Savings Plans available.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native teams building, training, and deploying custom models at scale with deep integration into the AWS ecosystem.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute/node-hour, prediction, and AutoML training; generative AI priced per token/character.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting highly automated, state-of-the-art AutoML and strong generative AI integration on GCP.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute/instance-hour and managed endpoints; no surcharge over underlying Azure compute; reserved instances available.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises in the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem needing governance, responsible AI, and integration with Azure OpenAI.

platforms.name: Databricks (MLflow + Mosaic AI)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based via Databricks Units (DBUs) plus underlying cloud compute; committed-use discounts available.
platforms.best_for: Collaborative data science teams with heavy data engineering/ETL needs wanting a unified multi-cloud lakehouse + ML platform.

platforms.name: Weights & Biases
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals/academics; paid per-seat and usage-based plans; enterprise self-hosted licensing.
platforms.best_for: ML research and engineering teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking and collaboration layered on any training stack.

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.best_for: Enterprises and business analysts wanting automated end-to-end AutoML with strong governance and low-code workflows.

platforms.name: H2O.ai
platforms.cloud: SaaS, multi-cloud, on-premises, and open source
platforms.pricing: Open-source core free; enterprise platform (H2O AI Cloud / Driverless AI) via subscription licensing.
platforms.best_for: Organizations wanting flexible open-source-friendly AutoML and generative AI with on-prem deployment options.

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.cloud: Serverless (runs on cloud GPUs, multi-cloud backend)
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per-second compute billing (CPU/GPU/memory); free starter credits.
platforms.best_for: Developers wanting serverless, code-first GPU compute for training and deploying models without managing infrastructure.

platforms.name: MLflow (open source)
platforms.pricing: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); costs only for self-hosted infrastructure.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting a free, framework-agnostic, open-source standard for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token/inference; provisioned throughput options for dedicated capacity.
platforms.best_for: Teams building generative AI applications on AWS using managed foundation models with fine-tuning and RAG, without managing training infrastructure.
